content: These conditions are not typically serious but can cause discomfort. Corns usually develop on the top or sides of toes, often as a result of poorly fitting shoes. For example, individuals who engage in activities like farming or rowing may develop calluses on their hands to prevent painful blisters. Similarly, people with bunions may develop calluses over the bunion due to constant rubbing against footwear. The symptoms of corns and calluses include areas of skin that are thickened, hardened, flaky, or dry. Diagnosis of corns and calluses is straightforward and is usually made by a healthcare provider through visual examination of the affected skin. In most cases, no additional tests are required. It is important to monitor your feet closely if you have diabetes or experience numbness in your feet or toes. If you have diabetes and notice any issues with your feet, you should contact your healthcare provider immediately. For most individuals, simply switching to better-fitting shoes or wearing gloves during activities that cause friction can resolve the problem. However, if a corn or callus becomes infected, or if symptoms such as pain, redness, warmth, or drainage persist despite treatment, you should seek medical attention. For corns caused by ill-fitting shoes, switching to properly fitting footwear can resolve the issue within a few weeks. In the meantime, donut-shaped corn pads, available at pharmacies, can protect the skin. A pumice stone can also be used to gently reduce the thickness of the corn. For calluses on the hands, wearing gloves during activities like gardening or weightlifting can help prevent further friction. If an infection or ulcer develops in the area of a corn or callus, a healthcare provider may need to remove unhealthy tissue and prescribe antibiotics. Calluses that result from underlying conditions, such as bunions, should be addressed by treating the root cause to prevent recurrence. Corns and calluses are rarely serious and, with proper treatment, typically resolve without causing long-term issues. However, individuals with diabetes are at higher risk for complications such as ulcers and infections. These individuals should regularly examine their feet and seek medical attention promptly if any problems are identified.
